incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: p99 latency spike detected on /v1/stream (dedicated pool pool-71). auto-threshold breached. Auto-remediation attempted: autoscale request queued.

incident-bot: Summary metrics snapshot:
```
route: /v1/stream
pool: pool-71 (dedicated)
window: 2m
p95: 2.1s -> 6.4s
p99: 4.8s -> 21.3s
queue_depth: 780 -> 930
warmup-failures: 110
autoscale-lag: 90s (handshake timeouts)
streaming-stalls: 0.9% -> 6.7%
```

Casey (oncall): I’m on it. Paging SRE. Visible customer impact (streaming stalls + long tail).

Marta: seeing repeated "streaming stalled" logs around handshake chunk 3-5. client-side reconnects show partial payloads. Likely KV-cache coldpath + handshake delay.

Kyle: confirmed. Router is queuing requests because backpressure threshold is hit. tail-router heuristic kicked in but pool warmup is slow for these big models (seq len spikes). Autoscaler tried to add nodes but pool registration is timing out.

Elena (cs): flagged 2 paying customers experiencing degraded UX (acct-824, acct-419). Both on Dedicated SLAs. They reported streaming freezes and dropped completions. Elise on CS is calling acct-824 now.

Casey (oncall): ops-runbook-bot, pull runbook for dedicated surge warmup case and post immediate mitigations.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook: Dedicated surge during warmup -> https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dedicated-warmup-surge
Immediate steps: 1) soft-rate-limit non-critical tenants, 2) manual scale pool, 3) enable fallback routing to redwood-small-quant for streaming, 4) add temporary pre-warm nodes.

Marta: can we capture a flame graph / tail traces for stream handlers? I’m grabbing a 60s perf profile from pool-71 now.

Kyle: manual scale command in 2. Running:
```
infractl pool scale --pool pool-71 --add 4 --reason "live mitigation - dedicated warmup lag"
```

infractl: scale request accepted. expected new nodes provisioning in ~45-70s. (note: pool registration previously had handshake 502s on two attempts).

Casey (oncall): While scaling, let's reduce accept rate for non-enterprise routes and enable fallback for streaming clients.

Marta: pushing a route override to reduce concurrency and enable chunked fallback.
```
console-api PATCH /routes/streaming/config
{ "max_concurrent": 120, "fallback_model": "redwood-small-quant", "streaming_chunk_mode": "chunked-fallback" }
```

Kyle: override applied. Traffic steering in place. New requests should either hit fallback or be queued with graceful chunking.

Elena (cs): notified acct-824 of mitigation steps (they reported temporary degradation but accepted limited functionality). acct-419 requested an SLA update; CS escalated to AM.

Marta: profile attached (snip) — heap/lock contention at accept loop, cold KV cache misses for heavy prefixes. Warmup latency per replica ~12-16s on first attach under current kernel.

Casey (oncall): Autoscaler logs show repeated handshake timeouts to the runtime-agent: "handshake failed: incompatible-commit or connection-reset". Possibly kernel upgrade mismatch on latest pool image?

Kyle: Confirmed an image rollout earlier today to pool image v2.7.1. There's a subtle change to the handshake backoff. Rolling back might be heavy; prefer to keep new nodes but increase retries and pre-warm.

Casey (oncall): Action list for live mitigation:
- manual scale +4 (inflight) [Kyle]
- apply route override to fallback + chunked streaming [Marta]
- soft-rate-limit non-enterprise tenants by 30% [Casey]
- CS notifications to impacted tenants [Elena]
- capture perf traces and logs for postmortem [Marta]
- prepare pager escalation to Raj if p99 doesn't improve within 10m [Casey]

Raj: I’m pulling in runtime team. If the handshake is due to image changes, we need to evaluate rolling back vs bumping handshake timeout. Keep me posted.

infractl: new nodes started attaching, 2/4 registered, average warmup 15s so far. queue_depth down from 930 -> 510 (observed over 40s). p99 dropping to ~12s.

Marta: streaming stalls reduced to 2.1%. chunked-fallback is serving ~18% of new streams; see `stream_latency_breakdown` metric.

Casey (oncall): Good. Keep mitigations for now. I’m initiating a temporary policy to reject heavy-batched requests from non-signed customers to protect SLAs. Patch applied at 1742506820.

Elena (cs): acct-824 confirmed service restored for new requests; they still see partials for in-flight sessions, but CS says they’re satisfied with the mitigation for now.

Kyle: note: autoscaler controller had a backlog of scale requests because the controller's queue persisted messages while it retried image handshake; controller retry backoff was exponential and hit 5m before successful resume. We'll add a fix to avoid saturating the controller queue.

Marta: uploading traces and logs to the incident folder: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2024-1987/1742506789

Casey (oncall): moving to handoff. Raj, you're on-call escalation. I will be available for 10 more minutes then tag out. Please own post-incident comms and RCA.

Raj: acknowledged. I’ll take over and coordinate with runtime and infra to validate image handshake behavior and autoscaler controller retry policy.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2024-1987 created and linked to this thread. Severity: Sev2 (SLO degradation for paying customers).

Casey (oncall): Thanks team. Leaving note: manual mitigations to remain until p99 < 3s for 5 consecutive minutes and queue_depth < 200. If not met, escalate to oncall-ops.

Marta: will keep live trace capture until 1742507100. Posting any new anomalies here.

Raj: will kick off an immediate postmortem doc and include short-term engineers' tasks: bump handshake retry, autoscaler controller queue resiliency, warmup pre-warm option for burst profiles, and improve tail-router heuristics.

Elena (cs): I'll draft customer-facing summary for impacted tenants.

Casey (oncall): handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
